entry.title: A basket of things to explore
entry.summary: For a baby who gets into sitting independently, the authors describe a discovery basket of a few varied objects, each suitable for grasping and mouthing with all parts secure.
entry.cue: Sitting leaves your baby’s hands free, and they are interested in choosing and examining objects.
detail: Their examples include a small group of kitchen objects with different shapes or textures. The baby chooses what to examine; an occasional name can fit without interrupting every discovery.
A separate appendix example uses two or three familiar toys in a soft basket while the baby lies or sits. That simpler choice is distinct from propping a baby to use a seated discovery basket.

references.section: Activities list for babies / Basket with known objects
references.locator: 5 or 6+ months, two or three familiar objects, lying or sitting

ageContext.bookAge: Main basket example: 6–9-month section after independent sitting. Familiar-object appendix basket: 5 or 6+ months.
ageContext.readiness: Independent sitting for the seated discovery basket; simple familiar-object variant also allows lying.
ageContext.note: The activity may continue while it fits your child’s interest and current skills; the source ages are guides.

displayContext.footer: You don’t need a different home. Start with what you have.
displayContext.colophon: Original summaries inspired by The Montessori Baby and The Montessori Toddler. Open any idea for its book references. The illustration is an invitation to explore, rather than a room to reproduce. Follow your child’s pace.
